charts.loss_description: Training or validation loss per epoch for each fold. Dashed vertical lines mark the best epoch.
charts.metrics_description: Selected metric per epoch for each fold. The dashed horizontal line shows the mean best F1.
charts.overfitting_description: Ratio of val_loss / train_loss per epoch. Values above 1 indicate potential overfitting.
charts.fold_summary_description: Best validation F1 and accuracy for each fold at the best epoch.

tooltips.optimizer: Adam for ResNet (proven fine-tuning baseline). AdamW for ConvNeXt and DINOv2 — decoupled weight decay prevents overfitting on small datasets.
tooltips.learning_rate: Fine-tuning LR from the model registry. ResNet: 0.001 (standard), ConvNeXt: 0.0001 (LayerNorm is sensitive to large gradients), DINOv2: 0.0002 (LoRA adapter).
tooltips.weight_decay: L2 regularization strength. 0 for ResNet (BatchNorm provides implicit regularization), 0.05 for ConvNeXt (ConvNeXt paper recipe), 0.01 for DINOv2 (light regularization on LoRA adapters).
tooltips.patience: Stops training after 15 consecutive epochs without val_loss improvement. Catches convergence without premature stopping.
tooltips.batch_size: Physical batch=8 (fits 4GB VRAM). Effective batch=32 via gradient accumulation (4 steps). Mathematically identical to batch=32 for cross-entropy loss.
tooltips.epochs: Maximum training duration. Early stopping terminates earlier via patience.
tooltips.test_accuracy: Overall fraction of correctly classified test images (300 total, 50 per class).
tooltips.f1_macro: Harmonic mean of per-class F1 scores. Preferred over accuracy for imbalanced datasets.

hero.title: OrchID-NCD
hero.description: An end-to-end research framework developed at the University of Naples Federico II for ultra-fine-grained visual classification and representation learning of Ophrys orchids.

vectorSpace.title: Structured Embedding Space
vectorSpace.description: We construct a high-dimensional vector space where morphologically similar orchid species cluster together via Supervised Contrastive Learning [8]. This latent representation enables similarity search, outlier detection, and provides the foundation for discovering previously unseen species.

ncd.title: Novel Class Discovery
ncd.description: Standard classifiers operate under a closed-world assumption. Our research tackles Novel Class Discovery [7]: can a model recognize that an unknown orchid does not belong to any known species, and group novel entities into meaningful clusters without supervision?

scientific.title: The Ophrys Problem
scientific.content1: The genus Ophrys is one of the most taxonomically challenging orchid groups in the Mediterranean. These orchids use sexual deception to attract species-specific pollinators, producing flowers that mimic female insects through visual cues, scent, and tactile signals [1].
scientific.content2: This extreme specialisation drives rapid morphological divergence and frequent hybridization, resulting in visually ambiguous specimens that challenge even expert botanists. The Ophrys sphegodes complex alone encompasses multiple cryptic taxa with overlapping phenotypic traits [2][3].

journey.title: Experimental Journey
journey.baselines: The first five experiments explored only ResNet18 (Exp 1–3) and ResNet50 (Exp 4–5) on standard train/val/test splits, using a combined dataset of private field photos and internet-sourced images across six Ophrys species of the sphegodes complex: O. exaltata, O. garganica, O. incubacea, O. majellensis, O. sphegodes, and O. sphegodes ssp. sphegodes (Palena population). Experiment 4 introduced 5-fold stratified cross-validation for both architectures, establishing the rigorous evaluation protocol still in use today. ConvNeXt and DINOv2 had not yet been tested.
journey.leakage: MD5 content hashing revealed that the train and test sets shared visually identical images under different filenames — a subtle form of data leakage that artificially inflated metrics and invalidated all results from Exp 1–5. The same orchid photograph, downloaded multiple times with different names, was present in both training and test partitions.
journey.preprocessing: The original pipeline applied aggressive center-cropping to a fixed resolution, destroying aspect ratio information. Since ResNet expects 256×512 inputs while ConvNeXt and DINOv2 use 224×224, the same crop produced distorted, information-poor inputs across architectures. We replaced this with letterbox resizing: images are scaled to fit within the target dimensions while preserving aspect ratio, with black padding bands filling the remaining space.
journey.clean: Experiment 6 is a complete restart on a deduplicated clean split with MD5-verified zero overlap between training (2,017 images) and test (300 balanced, 50 per class). For the first time, six architectures — ResNet18, ResNet50, ConvNeXt-Tiny, ConvNeXt-Small, DINOv2-Small, and DINOv2-Base — are evaluated with per-architecture input sizing and 5-fold stratified cross-validation.

model_selection.title: Architecture Comparison
model_selection.description: We benchmark three families of architectures to understand which inductive biases best capture subtle floral differences: ResNet (hierarchical local features via residual connections [4]), ConvNeXt (modernised CNN with large kernels and LayerNorm [5]), and DINOv2 (self-supervised Vision Transformer with global attention, trained on 142M images [6]).

optimization.title: Per-Architecture Recipes
optimization.description: Each architecture receives a tailored training recipe. DINOv2 is fine-tuned via LoRA adapters [9] (rank r=8, alpha=16, dropout=0.1) targeting the query and value projections of all attention layers, updating just ~0.5% of parameters while keeping the backbone frozen. ResNet uses Adam [10], while ConvNeXt and DINOv2 use AdamW with decoupled weight decay [11].

rigor.title: Experimental Rigor
rigor.description: All results are validated through 5-fold stratified cross-validation on a deduplicated clean split. MD5 hashing ensures zero content overlap between training and test sets, eliminating the data leakage that invalidated our preliminary experiments. Early stopping uses patience on val_loss. We evaluated the Generalization Loss criterion [12] but found it terminated training prematurely, before convergence.

augmentation.title: Balanced Augmentation
augmentation.description: Class imbalance is addressed per-fold: the minority class determines the target count, which is multiplied by the number of augmentation transforms (random flips, rotation, color jitter) to produce a balanced dataset where every class has the same number of training images.

future.title: Next Steps
future.phase2: Serie 2 will apply Supervised Contrastive Learning (SupCon) [8] to reshape the latent space, pulling same-class embeddings together while pushing different-class ones apart. This structured representation is the prerequisite for Novel Class Discovery.
future.phase3: Serie 3 will leverage the embedding space for nearest-neighbor retrieval, species clustering, and open-set recognition [7] — enabling the system to identify unknown orchid species in the wild.

footer.description: This project is part of a Master's Thesis on the application of Self-Supervised Learning and Novel Class Discovery to biodiversity data.
